content:
You can redefine LaTeX’s internal caption-making macro `\@makecaption`. This avoids using the `caption` package.

### Left-align all captions

Put this in your preamble:

```latex
\makeatletter
\long\def\@makecaption#1#2{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \noindent\raggedright
  #1: #2\par
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip
}
\makeatother
```

Example:

```latex
\documentclass{article}

\makeatletter
\long\def\@makecaption#1#2{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \noindent\raggedright
  #1: #2\par
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip
}
\makeatother

\begin{document}

\begin{table}
\caption{This is a left-aligned table caption.}
\centering
\begin{tabular}{cc}
A & B \\
1 & 2
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\end{document}
```

This will left-align captions for both tables and figures.

---

### Left-align only a single table caption

If you only want to affect one table, define the caption style locally inside that table:

```latex
\begin{table}
\makeatletter
\long\def\@makecaption#1#2{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \noindent\raggedright
  #1: #2\par
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip
}
\makeatother

\caption{This caption is left-aligned.}
\centering
\begin{tabular}{cc}
A & B \\
1 & 2
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
```

---

### For a very short caption only

For a one-off short caption, you can also do:

```latex
\caption{\makebox[\linewidth][l]{This caption is left-aligned.}}
```

But this will not wrap nicely if the caption is long, so the `\@makecaption` method is better.
